h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבַּת תְּשׁוּבָה, ח׳ Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 8

p: and said to him, 'What became of your judgment?'
He said to him, 'I did teshuvah and reached a settlement.'
הִתְחִיל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן מְטַפֵּחַ עַל פָּנָיו,
Adam HaRishon began striking his face
אָמַר כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי;
and said, 'Such is the power of teshuvah,' etc.;
immediately Adam HaRishon stood and said,
'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos.'"
וְכִי זֶהוּ רַק הַכֹּחַ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה,
is this all the power of teshuvah,
that is, for the punishment to be lightened by half,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ח, א, וְעוֹד)
as they said (Devarim Rabbah 8:1, and elsewhere)
that "na," wandering, was lightened from him,
Surely the true power of teshuvah
"It is not written here 'and I ate,'
I ate and I will eat."
Seemingly it is difficult to say
that he did not want to forsake his way,
but rather said that he would eat again.
that he could overcome his yetzer
after it had already entered him.
when he had no yetzer hara,
it was able to enter him and entice him,
he will certainly not prevail against it;
וְלֹא הָיָה רוֹצֶה לְרַמּוֹת אֶת בּוֹרְאוֹ.
and he did not want to deceive his Creator.
And this is what the Midrash says,
that he said "I ate and I will eat"
that he would certainly eat again.
that the essential definition of teshuvah is
פֶּרֶק ב מֵהִלְכוֹת תְּשׁוּבָה, הֲלָכָה ב)
until He Who knows hidden things testifies about him
that he will never return to this sin;
and this he did not trust himself,
שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יִצְרוֹ כָּל כָּךְ.
that he could overcome his yetzer to such an extent.
But after he heard from Kayin,
who told him, "I did teshuvah and reached a settlement,"
even though it is brought (Bereishis Rabbah ibid.)
that he went out like one deceiving the Supreme Mind,
that it is effective even with verbal confession alone,
even though he does not yet forsake the sin
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית ח, א):
This is along the lines of what they said (Taanis 8a):
and lied to Him with their tongue,' etc.,
'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos'";
that is, for there it is written,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem,"
"he who confesses and forsakes shall obtain mercy";
rather, this is the power of Shabbos:
that words alone will also be effective.
This is like what the Rambam wrote
on the reason a coerced get is valid in Yisrael:
אַף שֶׁהוּא בֶּאֱמֶת אָנוּס עַל יְדֵי זֶה,
although he is truly compelled by this,
and if the compulsion were removed from him
But since he is truly obligated,
only his yetzer has overpowered him
and it is his yetzer that overpowered him,
once he was beaten until his yetzer was weakened
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז, א):
This is based on what they said (Berachos 17a):
"It is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will;
הוּא לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת.
is to do the will of Hashem, blessed be He, completely.
that Yisrael are bound at the root
and that our will is to do Your will,
even confession of the mouth is effective.
And this is why we say,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem."
And so we find with Kayin
that his teshuvah truly was effective,
that Naamah was the wife of Noach;
and from her came forth the whole world,
and Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
and the entire nation of Yisrael.
Likewise regarding the root of souls,
it is brought from the holy Arizal
that half are from the root of Kayin
and half from the root of Hevel.
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַשַּׁבָּת;
This too is through the power of Shabbos;
for at the onset of Shabbos it is written,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good,"
as referring to everything that is the opposite of good.
This is as we have said
and where do we find creation in connection with evil?
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים נד, א):
But it is based on what they said (Pesachim 54a):
לָמָּה לֹא נֶאֱמַר כִּי טוֹב בַּשֵּׁנִי?
"Why is 'that it was good' not said on the second day?
Because there was created on it
And we have said that the fire of Gehinnom
which is the fire of Gehinnom,
but a fire that comes forth
from the bodies of the wicked," etc.;
that is, the fire of desire;
"that it was good" is not said of it.
"'Not good' means nothing other than evil."
But at the onset of Shabbos it is written,
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה
"And God saw all that He had made,
and behold, it was very good."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
This is based on what they said in the holy Zohar
אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּלֵּי,
except that which comes forth from within darkness," etc.,
except that which comes forth from within evil."
And this is revealed on Shabbos,
Therefore Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
when even Kayin's teshuvah was effective.
"A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos:
It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
שֶׁיְּבָרֵר אוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אַחַר כָּךְ
for Hashem, blessed be He, will afterward make clear regarding him
that it truly comes from the will of the heart,
that our will is to do Your will,
in the very beginning of Thought,
